conventions.signs: z>0 is the positive-energy Maxwell sign; the claim-1603 scalar convention is recovered at z=0 with a>0,b>0
conventions.completeness: up to integration by parts, S^2, (partial.S)^2 and F^2 span the flat-space parity-even quadratic axial-vector action with at most two derivatives

spin1Transverse.canonicalForm: for z>0 and a=-z m_1^2, A_mu=sqrt(z)S_mu gives L=-F_A^2/4-m_1^2 A^2/2

healthConditions.simultaneousDecision: NO OPEN REGION: healthy spin-1 requires a<0 while healthy spin-0 requires a>0
healthConditions.failureForScalarHealthySigns: a>0,b>0,z>0 gives a healthy 0-minus scalar but m_1^2<0, so the transverse vector is tachyonic
healthConditions.failureForVectorHealthySigns: a<0,z>0 and b<0 gives positive masses for both poles, but the longitudinal scalar has negative kinetic norm

generic_bz_nonzero.spectrum: three massive transverse spin-1 polarizations plus one longitudinal spin-0 mode

z_zero_scalar_surface.radiativeStatus: not stable once fermions with nonzero axial coupling generate F^2

constraintCounts.a_zero: rank-changing massless surface; with b and z nonzero the velocity Hessian is full rank but the Maxwell-plus-divergence system carries an indefinite unprotected four-component kinetic sector, not a continuous healthy limit

nonconservedAxialCurrent.wardIdentity: p.J_5,f=2m_f times the pseudoscalar density plus gauge anomalies
nonconservedAxialCurrent.decision: massive fermions and anomalies expose the longitudinal pole; current conservation cannot be used to hide its ghost or tachyon
nonconservedAxialCurrent.conservedLimit: an exactly conserved external current has p.J=0 and does not exchange the scalar, but this source restriction does not remove the scalar from the spectrum
nonconservedAxialCurrent.lowMomentum: K^{-1}=eta/a+(p^2/a^2)(z P_T-b P_L)+O(p^4), so both sectors share the algebraic J^2/a contact at leading order

decouplingSurfaces: z=0: the transverse pole becomes algebraic and the healthy claim-1603 0-minus scalar surface is recovered
b=0: the longitudinal pole becomes algebraic and an ordinary healthy Proca surface exists for z>0,a<0
b=z=0: all axial torsion is algebraic
J=0: matter exchange vanishes but the free pole health problem remains
p.J=0: longitudinal exchange vanishes for that source only
a=0: constraint/pole rank changes and neither massive health criterion can be continued through the surface

finiteScan.statement: the scan is a finite witness of the analytic sign contradiction, not its proof

spin23InvariantMap.a: Einstein-Cartan plus broken-phase torsion squares; in the one-lambda truncation a=M_Pl^2(1-4lambda)/24
spin23InvariantMap.b: the parity-even square of the Riemann-Cartan pseudoscalar curvature Xhat, whose linear axial part is partial.S
spin23InvariantMap.z: a complementary linear combination of parity-even Riemann-Cartan curvature-square invariants whose axial quadratic projection contains F_S^2; fermion vacuum polarization generates the same allowed operator
spin23InvariantMap.warning: a generic curvature-square invariant also activates trace torsion, tensor torsion and/or metric sectors; z cannot be treated as an isolated UV coefficient without an explicit irreducible-curvature projection
remainingFullSectors: trace-vector and tensor-torsion blocks and their mixings
metric curvature-square scalar and massive spin-2 blocks
constraint-critical surfaces that can remove modes but are not open generic regions

decision: The most general isolated parity-even two-derivative axial-vector completion has no open parameter region in which its massive spin-1 and spin-0 poles are both healthy. The shared algebraic coefficient a must have opposite signs. Healthy theories exist only on decoupling/critical surfaces that remove one pole, or potentially in a larger Poincare-gauge system whose mixings and constraints must be analyzed afresh.
stopRules: Reject every generic b*z!=0 point as a simultaneous healthy 1-plus/0-minus completion: it contains a transverse tachyon, a scalar ghost/tachyon, or a Maxwell ghost.
Retain z=0 only as a low-energy scalar EFT surface, not a radiatively closed fermion-coupled theory.
Retain b=0,z>0,a<0 as the healthy Proca decoupling surface, not as continuity with the healthy 0-minus branch.
Do not cross a=0 using massive pole formulas; the rank and constraint structure changes.
Do not infer health of the full broken Spin(2,3) curvature-square action from the axial projection; repeat the complete spin-parity and constraint analysis.
